summary.headline: Q1 FY27 total income INR250 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA INR44 crore (+27%), margin 17.5%; company entering AI data-centre business via GScale (up to 51%).
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR250 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA of INR44 crore (+27%), PBT of INR36 crore (+26%) and PAT of INR26 crore (+26%), with EBITDA margin at 17.5%. Two strategic moves were announced: acquisition of up to 51% in GScale Energy (AI data-centre power, cooling and skid products) and a ~19% stake in GL Hakko Japan for ~INR71 crore, with a right to rise to 51%. Management guided core business revenue to ~INR1,200 crore (+40-50%) and GScale to ~INR250 crore in FY27. Many forward figures (GScale revenue, margins, FY28) were left unquantified and deferred to future guidance.

segments.name: Core engineering (pharma, chemical, CDMO glass-lining)
segments.commentary: Guided to grow 40-50% in FY27 to ~INR1,200 crore; CDMO is ~50% of the unexecuted order book, balance pharma and chemicals. Management says it is moving to solutions sales, with no product-vs-turnkey split disclosed.

segments.name: GScale Energy (AI data-centre products and turnkey)
segments.commentary: Targeting ~INR250 crore revenue (management clarified revenue, not bookings) by end-FY27; five customers in advanced discussions (three global MNCs, two Indian). Expects 23-25% EBITDA margin and ~20% ROCE on ~INR500 crore investment; plant ~4 lakh sq ft, first phase operational by November.

segments.name: GL Hakko (Japan glass-lining technology partner)
segments.commentary: GL Hakko revenue ~INR200 crore; target INR400 crore in 2-3 years. Shell-and-tube glass-lining heat exchangers already being made in India (80% built in Japan, 20% finished locally); exports planned from FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance ~INR1,450 crore (core ~INR1,200 crore plus GScale ~INR250 crore).
Core business growth guided at 40-50% for FY27, up from earlier 25-30% minimum; management excluded current order book from the change.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at 17-18% going forward; GScale margin expected 23-25%.
Working capital days to fall below 200 in FY27 (September-half expected), and GScale targeted at 100-150 days.
GScale data-centre projects targeted at 18-20 months versus 24-36 months industry typical; ROCE expected ~20%.
FY28 GScale and consolidated revenue guidance deferred ('we will guide soon'); no quantified margin expansion from semiconductor glass-lining yet.
capex_capacity: GScale has acquired ~4 lakh sq ft factory space; ~2 lakh sq ft in full execution with robotic equipment ordered from multiple countries, arriving by mid-September.
GScale operations targeted to start by November 2026; further 2 lakh sq ft (factories 3 and 4) to be added by December 2026.
Total GScale investment cited at ~INR500 crore.
Management said full-fledged manufacturing setup to be complete around March (2027).
Manufacturing mix: GScale to make 60-70% of equipment in-house and source the balance; management says this can be increased.
Semiconductor-grade glass-lining reactors: glass sourced from Japan, fabrication and glass spraying in India; no technology transfer agreement currently.
demand_pricing: Management cites India data-centre capacity of 1.8 GW expected to grow to ~10.2-10.5 GW by ~2030-31; investment of USD5-7 million per MW, of which ~65% is products and installation.
GScale has one big order from a top Indian client for semiconductor-related glass-lining reactors (GL Hakko-linked); pilot-plant order for LED/electronic chemicals also cited.
Shell-and-tube glass-lining heat exchanger price cut claimed: from ~INR30 lakh to ~INR12-15 lakh per unit (>50% lower), with management arguing it is a client benefit and margin-accretive.
India glass-lining TAM cited at ~INR1,500 crore; shell-and-tube heat exchanger TAM ~INR2,000 crore in India and ~USD2 billion globally.
Management claims no global competitor makes the GL Hakko shell-and-tube glass-lining heat exchanger or low-leaching glass; unverified.
Export share remained low at 2-3% in Q1 due to global uncertainty; shipping costs cited by an analyst as up ~4x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the GScale business, margins, and timing of order conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Brahma Reddy said five customers (three global MNCs, two Indian) are in LOI or near-order stage; target is ~INR250 crore revenue by end-FY27, clarified as revenue not order booking. Margin guided at 23-25% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Margin expansion from semiconductor glass-lining products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will rise slightly as shell-and-tube and semiconductor products scale from September, but gave no quantified figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an unexecuted order book for core business?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, ~INR1,400 crore after Q1 billing, with some billing expected in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin down and is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to mechanisation in two units, which reduced consumable consumption; employee costs rising with recruitment. Management said margins will be maintained at 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days and drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said days were ~320 last year, targeted below 200 by September, driven by customer advances and receivable collection with stock held flat.

qa_highlights.question: Royalty on imported technology?
qa_highlights.answer: No royalty currently; licensing model, with JV and technology-transfer discussions ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre project timelines and value-add?
qa_highlights.answer: Typical industry project 24-36 months; GScale targets 18-20 months. Customers may free-issue some long-lead items; the 60% in-house share can be increased.

risks_watch: GScale execution: equipment arrival (mid-September), November start, and ramp to INR250 crore revenue in FY27 with only ~2 lakh sq ft initially in full execution.
Working capital: management's <200 day target versus ~320 days last year; GScale projects may carry advances and receivables.
Margin pressure: the 17.5% EBITDA margin reflects rising employee and other costs; management says 17-18% is sustainable.
Dependence on GL Hakko technology: critical glass manufacturing remains in Japan with no technology transfer agreement; GL Hakko stake to step up to 51% only on targets.
Forward guidance gaps: FY28 numbers for GScale and consolidated revenue not yet guided; a Q&A figure of ~INR3,000 crore for FY28 was not confirmed by management.
Customer concentration: GScale's five named-stage customers are unnamed; claims of no global competitor are unverified.
key_quotes: This has been another record quarter for us, and I want to say this clearly , this is not a one-time achievement.
Working capital days I think last year 320 days, 320 days. And this year we are that is going to coming down to below 200 days.
Brahma Reddy: We will guide soon.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on GScale and GL Hakko growth, with strong claims on uniqueness and market size. Cautious and evasive on FY28 numbers, the GScale margin bridge, and the semiconductor margin uplift, which were deferred ("we will guide soon", "we are working on that").
